clue.text: Raillery popular during naughty era

indicators.note: during places one piece within the span of another, so popular sits inside the naughty era

parts.note: naughty means bad
an era is an age
in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: Teasing banter becomes fashionable in a decadent period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts IN inside BAD AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean playful teasing talk, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Attendant, right with notion about sergeant major being in command

indicators.note: being in means the earlier pieces sit inside the word for command

parts.note: bid means to command, as in 'do as I bid'

indicators.note: about means the notion goes round the sergeant major

parts.note: an idea is a notion

explanation.surface: A soldier's aide with the right idea about the sergeant major who is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SM inside IDEA to make IDESMA; 'being in' puts R plus that inside BID.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridesmaid accompanies the bride, an attendant at a wedding.

clue.text: Movement after endless indecisiveness is embracing two gods

indicators.note: after places the movement behind the other pieces in the answer
endless means the word for indecisiveness loses its final letter

parts.note: dither is nervous indecision
a tic is an involuntary movement

explanation.surface: A twitch after long dithering is a sign of embracing two faiths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts DITHER to DITHE. The definition is adjectival, 'embracing two gods'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditheism is belief in two supreme deities, so a ditheistic faith holds a pair of them.

clue.text: Man, new one on stage, rising

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, so backwards
on in a down clue puts the new one below the stage before the whole is turned upwards

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A newcomer on stage gets up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed beneath, so the stage comes first; 'rising' then reads the whole thing upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigel is a man's name; crosswords use 'man' for any male forename.

clue.text: Artist gets boisterous, holding outside broadcast up

indicators.note: holding means the two outer words keep the broadcast between them

parts.note: gains means gets
rough means boisterous, as in rough play

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: A painter gets rowdy while hanging on to a TV broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns OB into BO, which 'holding' puts between GAINS and ROUGH. Thomas Gainsborough was an 18th-century English portrait painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gainsborough painted 'The Blue Boy', an English artist of the 1700s.

clue.text: Rascal by river getting dirty

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child, a rascal
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A naughty child playing by the river gets filthy.
explanation.walkthrough: The URE is a river in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impure is unclean or contaminated, a synonym of dirty.

clue.text: Dream's ending with horse surrounded by weird collection of animals

indicators.note: ending picks the end letter of the word dream
surrounded by means the horse sits inside the word for weird

parts.note: eerie means weird
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A dream ends with a horse ringed by a strange collection of beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounded by' puts NAG inside EERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a group of wild animals kept for show.

clue.text: Open wreck

definitions.meaning: to unfasten or unwrap a parcel
to ruin or destroy, as when one mistake can bring down a career

explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten something is to open it, and to ruin someone is to bring about their downfall.

clue.text: Regular occurrence: temperature's dropped

indicators.note: 's dropped means has been removed, so the temperature letter is taken out

parts.note: an event is an occurrence

explanation.surface: A regular happening once the temperature falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' removes T from EVENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular surface is smooth and level, so uniform in that sense.

clue.text: Carving-interested in receiving a good large one?

indicators.note: receiving means one piece takes the others inside it

parts.note: to be into something is to be interested in it
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Someone keen on getting a large, good piece of sculpture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' puts A, G, L and I inside INTO.
explanation.definitionFit: An intaglio is a design incised into stone or gem, a kind of engraved carving.

clue.text: Tense person brought before magistrate missing nothing

indicators.note: brought before places the person ahead of the magistrate in the answer

parts.note: one means a person, as in 'one never knows'

indicators.note: missing means the zero letter is taken out of the official's title

parts.note: the doge was the chief magistrate of Venice
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A nervous defendant waits to appear before the bench.
explanation.walkthrough: The DOGE was the elected chief magistrate of Venice; 'missing nothing' drops its O to leave DGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on edge is an idiom for feeling nervous and anxious.

clue.text: Time consumed by revision of so-so, insipid arrangements

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed inside the rearranged letters
revision of means the next words are reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Time is wasted revising a mediocre, dull set of arrangements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revision of' rearranges SOSO INSIPID into DISPOSIIONS and 'consumed by' puts T inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispositions are the way things are laid out, an alternative word for layouts.

clue.text: Endless alerts given in error

indicators.note: in error says the letters are wrongly arranged and must be put right

explanation.surface: Constant warnings issued by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in error' rearranges ALERTS GIVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everlasting never stops, a synonym of endless.

clue.text: What's one seen in prim aunts, possibly?

definitions.text: What's one seen in prim aunts, possibly?

indicators.note: seen in means the one is placed inside the other letters
possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A question about what quality you might spot in strait-laced maiden aunts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges PRIM AUNTS and 'seen in' puts I among them. The whole clue is also the definition: prim aunts would show strict morality.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict moral austerity is what prudish relatives are said to display.

clue.text: Revealing picture created by books about church after church

indicators.note: after says the books and church come behind the other church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
NT is the New Testament, books of the Bible
re means about, as in business letters
a fold is a flock of believers, the church

explanation.surface: Scandalous pin-up produced by holy books concerning the church.
explanation.walkthrough: FOLD, a shepherd's pen, stands for a church's flock. CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A centrefold is a nude pin-up photo across a magazine's middle pages, so a revealing image.

clue.text: Find Greek character so able to show what bouzouki's for?

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
sic is Latin for so or thus, printed to show a quotation is exact

explanation.surface: A Greek person able to show what their stringed instrument is for.
explanation.walkthrough: A bouzouki is a Greek lute; 'Greek character' suggests a person but is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A bouzouki is an instrument, and instruments exist to make melody and song.

clue.text: Working party whose members can't escape being linked with it?

definitions.text: Working party whose members can't escape being linked with it?

parts.words: Working party whose members can't escape being linked with it?
parts.note: a work gang of prisoners shackled together, so linked literally, not just associated

explanation.surface: A committee whose members are forever associated with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working party' suggests a committee and 'linked' an association, but the convicts are joined by iron.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain gang is a group of convicts fettered together while doing labour.

clue.text: Good work with opening that has devotee coming back, enthralled

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: enthralled means held captive, so the devotee is held within the opening

parts.note: a pore is a small opening in the skin

indicators.note: coming back means the word for the devotee is read backwards

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast or devotee

explanation.surface: A fine composition opening with a returning fan who is captivated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns NUT into TUN, which 'enthralled' puts inside PORE to make PORTUNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something opportune is well timed and suitable, so good in that sense.

clue.text: Mimics, funny sort, aim to retain appeal

indicators.note: to retain means to keep something within, so the appeal is held inside
funny suggests something odd, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: it means sex appeal, as in the old 'It girl'

explanation.surface: Impressionists, an amusing kind, try to keep the audience charmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' rearranges SORT AIM into IMATORS, which 'to retain' wraps around IT; IT is old slang for sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimics are people who copy others, the same as imitators.

clue.text: Order in Vedic texts

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of letters in the next words

explanation.surface: A command found in ancient Hindu scriptures.
explanation.walkthrough: The Vedas are ancient Hindu scriptures.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official decree, a formal order.

clue.text: Drink taken round, accompanied by sound of bell, carried by robust nurse

indicators.note: taken round means the drink's name is turned to face the other way

parts.note: gin is a spirit, a drink

indicators.note: carried by means held inside the following word for robust

parts.note: hale means healthy and robust
ting is the light ringing sound of a bell

explanation.surface: A sturdy nurse brings round drinks to the ring of a bell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken round' turns GIN into NIG; 'carried by' puts TING inside HALE. Florence Nightingale was the founder of modern nursing.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence Nightingale, the Crimean War nurse, is the archetype of the profession.

clue.text: Snare suggested by informer capturing ring

indicators.note: capturing means the informer holds the ring inside

parts.note: a nose is slang for a police informer
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A trap set by a grass who catches a gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capturing' puts O inside NOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop that tightens, used as a snare to trap.

clue.text: King, beginner of awful custom? It should be abandoned

indicators.note: beginner of picks the opening letter of awful
should be abandoned means that word is removed from the custom

parts.note: a habit is a custom

explanation.surface: A king starts a terrible practice that ought to be stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should be abandoned' takes IT from HABIT to leave HAB. Ahab was a wicked king of Israel in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahab ruled the northern kingdom of Israel, a biblical monarch.

clue.text: In past, sardonic one with great authority

indicators.note: In says the answer sits inside the run of letters in the next words

explanation.surface: Historically, a mocking person with great power.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the Russian emperor, an autocratic ruler.

clue.text: Soldier getting fish with a spear's extremity

parts.note: huss is a name for dogfish sold as food

indicators.note: extremity points to the end letter of the word for the weapon

explanation.surface: A soldier spears a fish with the tip of his lance.
explanation.walkthrough: HUSS is a British fishmonger's name for dogfish.
explanation.definitionFit: A hussar is a light cavalryman, a kind of soldier.

clue.text: Expression of disapproval about a gun in battle

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jeer goes round the other pieces

parts.note: boo is a jeer of disapproval
rod is American slang for a gun

explanation.surface: Jeering at a weapon used in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ROD and IN inside BOO. Borodino was the 1812 battle between Napoleon and the Russians.
explanation.definitionFit: Borodino is the site of the bloody 1812 clash outside Moscow, so a named battle.

clue.text: Plant with black fruit having no name

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: having no means the letter for name is removed from the fruit

parts.note: an orange is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A plant with dark berries that has never been named.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no' takes N from ORANGE to leave ORAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Borage is a blue-flowered herb, a kind of plant.

clue.text: Energy shown by horse going round the writer admired

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

indicators.note: going round means the horse surrounds the word for the writer

parts.note: a steed is a horse
the writer means the setter, referring to self as me

explanation.surface: An energetic horse circling the author is much admired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' puts ME inside STEED to make STEEMED; 'the writer' is the setter, so ME.
explanation.definitionFit: To be esteemed is to be held in high regard, a synonym of admired.
